justification: Vote 1, native read-aloud of title, passage (five paragraphs), five prompts, twenty options and five rationales, with every fleet-repair-1 string read in its new context rather than checked as a diff. The passage remains edited-weekly prose of real quality and the three rewritten quoted lines now read as people talking (six contractions across three speakers, ‘in any room’, ‘a range, not a number’). But the Cattermay rewrite severed an echo the writer had built: para 3 opens ‘Trevor Cottam … says the something else is nearly the whole of it’, a definite nominalisation that only works if ‘something else’ has just been said, and the new quote says ‘Something happened’. A reader hits ‘the something else’, asks ‘else than what?’, goes back and finds nothing — an unresolvable reference in the passage of a reading-comprehension item, which is the repair-fixes-the-named-string-and-breaks-the-neighbour pattern the brief warned of. Lethal by the gate’s standard (a native professional writer would not produce it), so kill. Second: the ‘go above’ garden path was replaced with ‘go ahead of’, which garden-paths harder; grammatical, so flag. Third, minor: Q3-A’s ‘earlier than the first minutes were put’. Considered and cleared: ‘has earned a quality payment in any quarter when’ (rule-plus-record present perfect, idiomatic); ‘takes a manufacturer’s ninety seconds’ (marked, deliberate, legible); ‘the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well’ (the new verdict sentence is native and better than the one it replaced); all six re-cut options read as native; the Q4 option set (‘show little and her explanation still less’, ‘though not by how much’) is idiomatic English; ‘the clerk’-style repetition does not arise here. OUT OF G-ENG SCOPE but recorded for the integrated read: para 3 ‘five of the nine added minutes only brought the book level with the boat’ against a median of twenty-four on an eighteen-minute booking (six), and the rationales’ own ‘six minutes over the book’ / ‘six of the nine added minutes’ — a pre-existing number inconsistency, not touched by the repair.

Vote 1, native read-aloud of the gapped passage with the keys inserted, five gap prompts, twenty options and five rationales, with particular weight on the two repaired frames (gap 3 and gap 5) and the extended gap-4 sentence. Nothing a native writer would not produce. The gap-4 frame now reads ‘she concedes that in August they are an interruption and by late September most of the job, a description rather than a complaint’: ‘interruption’ is the right noun (r1’s ‘obstruction’ is gone) and the summative appositive over the reported clause is a normal English move; it is compressed, but the misattachment to ‘most of the job’ fails on sense at once and the intended reading takes over, so it clears. Gap 3 with the key inserted — ‘The hire is the whole of the transaction … In practice, the pitch is the one staffed thing on the mile’ — is idiomatic; ‘In addition’ and ‘In short’ are both live sentence-initial connectives, so the set no longer halves on shape, and neither reads as exotic English. Gap 5: ‘barely used’ is the native fill. ‘scantily used’, judged as asked: NOT a live collocation — ‘scantily’ pairs with clad, dressed, furnished, covered, populated (quantity provided), never with frequency of use; the live minimisers before ‘used’ are little, barely, hardly, scarcely, seldom, rarely, sparsely. So it is exotic, which is exactly the distractor design (grammatical slot, dead pairing) and not a second key; it is not a G-ENG defect because it never enters the passage. ‘strongly used’ likewise dead by design. Texture is the best in the batch and untouched: ‘It thins, and then one week the chairs stay in’, ‘the tin took four pounds forty’, ‘a thing you ask of somebody who will still be there’, ‘a chair you have paid for has done the approaching for you’. Considered and cleared: non-backshift in ‘she said it is because she stands still and they do not’ (journalistic present for a standing truth); ‘well signed’ (BrE, alongside ‘signposted’); the gapping ‘and Carol Gregson the one person on it who is stationary and paid’.

Vote 1, native read-aloud of title, passage, prompt, the fully rebuilt four-option set and the rewritten rationale, with the two renamed figures read in place. Passage untouched apart from the given names, and Gordon Hoskadale / Fiona Hebden sit in it as unremarkable British names; ‘Gordon Hoskadale went up two mesh sizes in his cod end’ scans as the old line did. The prose remains unmistakably native (‘waited for the small haddock to see themselves out’, ‘A whole spring on’, ‘turned right round the bag’, the absolute ‘a flat fish and a stretched mesh being much the same shape’, ‘on the tows when the square bars ran slack’). The rebuilt options read as English a gear-page sub-editor would write: A ‘He judged the larger meshes on the catch from a single trip’ (judge X on Y, native); B ‘Once the meshes were turned, the plaice no longer got out, a flat fish being the wrong shape for a square’ (absolute construction echoing the passage’s own, natural); C ‘The way the netting hung was the first thing he changed in the bag’; D ‘Towing narrowed the meshes, so the extra size did not give a round fish its width’ — r1 vote 1’s ‘closed’ -> ‘narrowed’ is DISCHARGED and the key verb now matches the passage’s slot mechanism; the singular/plural inconsistency r1 found between old A and D is gone with old A. The rationale’s new glosses are fluent (‘supplies a trip where the text has a season’, ‘rules out in so many words’, ‘hangs on it a change in the plaice’, ‘checked against the page’). QUOTED VOICE: four short coordinate sentences, generic ‘you’, deck-anchored, a working aphorism; it reads as a fisherman quoted in a trade paper. No contraction is taken (‘A net is one thing’, ‘A haddock is round’), but both copulas are stressed in aphoristic speech and would be said uncontracted, so this is not the composed-prose tell; cleared, concurring with r1 vote 1. Nothing to record.

Vote 1, native read-aloud of title, passage, prompt, four options and the rationale, with the two repaired strings read in context. The passage holds under the ear exactly as before: ‘John Ward was bound twice’, the semicolon ellipsis ‘in 1755 to a whitesmith, for seven years again, and fourteen pounds’, the fronted object ‘and one the clerk left unplaced’. The repaired final sentence, ‘The clerk set his fee of two shillings against each enrolment, and twice against Ward’s name’, resolves at once; the cost is ‘the clerk left unplaced. The clerk set’ in adjacent sentences, a repetition a local-history essayist would accept for clarity over a four-referent reach — cleared. Option D, ‘The five went into their second trades for a smaller premium than they had paid the first time’, is now a parallel comparison (premium against premium); ‘they had paid’ gives the boys loose agency for a sum a father put down, which the passage itself leaves unassigned (‘with eleven pounds paid down’), so it reads as ordinary English compression, not error. Options A–C unchanged and native (‘bound for years beyond the day their first term would have ended’, ‘lost their first places’, ‘placed a second time by families living in the town’). The rationale’s rewritten opening, ‘KEY A. The passage states four things and joins none of them’, is prose; the arithmetic sentence (‘must still be running when the first term would have expired, and must run three to six years past it’) is correct English and correct arithmetic. Considered and cleared: ‘naming Ward’s father, his trade and his parish’ (the ‘his’ is ambiguous between Ward and the father, but that is how real enrolment-register prose reads and a native writer would produce it). Nothing to record.
